item.title: 25 of my favourite modern NES games – The Scribbler of the Rueful Countenance
item.description: We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it.

item.title: Someone's impersonating this blog — A Lovely Harmless Monster – Blog
item.description: I was googling the name of my website, as one does occasionally, and was surprised to see a link to one of my blog posts on mataroa.site. At first I figured it was just an alternate domain name for mataroa.blog, but no, when you type mataroa.site into your browser, it shows you my blog. It's the only thing that's hosted there.

item.title: The MacBook Pro’s OLED PWM Problem: When a ‘Better’ Display Becomes Worse to Use
item.description: Apple has made a spectacular display. But spectacular isn’t the same as comfortable, and the people discovering that distinction deserve to be heard.

item.title: We’re Asking an Appeals Court to Require a Warrant for ALPR Searches
item.description: Automated license plate readers are simply not comparable to observing an individual license plate on a passing car. As we’ve explained in many amicus briefs and in our lawsuits directly challenging their use, ALPRs give law enforcement “a virtual time machine to view suspects’, or anyone else’s, past movements (and much more) with just the click of a button.”

item.title: Running a law firm on Free software (2026 edition)
A Family Tree of Software Job Titles – zwischenzugs.com
item.description: For a few years I was ‘Head of DevOps’. Before I got that job title I’d done much the same work under other names, and since then I’ve watched the same work get called SRE, and then it seemed to morph towards platform engineering. If you’ve been in this industry for any length of time you’ll have seen titles come and go like this, and you might have wondered where they all came from.

item.title: Advertising Two Pi-hole DNS IP Addresses via DHCP | no dogma blog
item.description: If your Pi-hole has two IP addresses on eth0 handling DNS, you can get its DHCP to advertise both addresses. This might block the client from using hardcoded secondary DNS IP addresses that would bypass the Pi-hole.
